title: Maximum Number of Points with Cost
summary: Given an m x n matrix of integers, determine the maximum score by selecting one cell per row.
statement: Given an m x n matrix of integers, determine the maximum score by selecting one cell per row. Each selected cell's value is added to the score, but points are deducted for the distance between cells in adjacent rows. The distance is the absolute difference in column indices. The task is to find the highest possible score.
constraints: points is a nonempty rectangular matrix with at most 100000 cells.
Select exactly one cell per row and subtract the absolute column change between adjacent selections.
hints: For each destination column, the previous-row transition separates into a best value from the left and from the right.
Sweep left while maintaining max(previous[c]+c), then right with max(previous[c]-c).
For every row compute both directional maxima, add the current cell, and retain the larger transition.
The two sweeps partition every predecessor by whether it lies left or right of the destination and algebraically include the exact absolute-distance penalty.
editorial: The two sweeps partition every predecessor by whether it lies left or right of the destination and algebraically include the exact absolute-distance penalty.

tests.explanation: Columns two, one, and zero score 3+5+3 minus two moves, for nine.
Columns one, one, and zero score twelve before one movement point, for eleven.
